- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.33) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–20% for early horizon (1–7 days) and 30–50% for mid/late horizon (8–30 days).  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 3x recent mean), model often overcorrects downward; apply a “lag correction” — reduce forecast by 20–40% for 3–5 days post-spike.  
- If sentiment is high (≥0.67) and price is trending up, model underestimates upside; increase forecast by 10–25% for 1–5 days, then apply mean reversion to 1.5x recent average after 7 days.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently overestimates in high-sentiment periods; apply a “sentiment decay” rule: multiply forecast by 0.85–0.95 if sentiment > 0.67 over last 5 days.  
- If sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and price is volatile, model exhibits “mean reversion bias” — forecast should be capped at 1.2x recent 7-day average to avoid over-oscillation.
